What you are looking at Kello shows where each wellbeing services county loses lung cancer patients between diagnosis and treatment that aims to cure, and what closes that gap. The care path comes from the Finnish Cancer Registry's own county figures. The plan is Kello's: a list of actions with an owner, a cost, a first step and a measure, chosen by stated rules. Public aggregate data only; no patient-level data. Three kinds of number Measured. Taken directly from a public source. Estimated. Produced by the model, shown with an interval. Assumption. Set by hand where no data exists; editable. An estimate is never shown as a measurement. Every estimate carries a range, written like 0–7.7. Every number on screen has a chip that opens this panel at its source. How Kello reads reports The Finnish Cancer Registry publishes county results as PDF reports and interactive pages with no API. Gemini reads each document page by page and returns every number with its page and a verbatim quote. A second pass looks for each number again on its page. Not verified means the second pass did not find the number again in the same words, usually because the page shows it in a chart or a rounded table cell. Those values stay in Kello, marked as unverified wherever they appear. Added by you, unverified Nothing yet. In the Plan view, “Read a report” lets you read any report and add single values to Kello; they are listed here. Method, in plain language The care path. For each county the registry publishes how many lung cancer patients were staged, discussed by a team, treated to cure, operated, given other treatment or have no treatment on record. Kello shows each share with its 95% range, next to Finland and the best county. Beyond chance. A small county's share moves a lot from one period to the next. Kello draws the range that chance alone gives a county of each size around the national share, and only calls a county lower or higher when it is outside that range. Missing patients. The county's share against the national share, times its patients a year. It is arithmetic on registry shares: it does not say which patients could have been treated to cure. Expected share. What the county's share would be if only the age of its residents mattered. Stage, fitness and other illness are not published by county and cannot be adjusted for. Actions. Each action has an assumed effect with a low and a high end, taken from published studies in other health systems, a cost assumption and an owner. No trial has measured the access effects in Finland, so their low end is zero. The plan. For a budget, Kello chooses the actions that add the most patients treated to cure per euro, within stated rules. Every rule is listed on the county page under “How this was chosen”. The estimated clock, and a check that did not confirm it Kello also estimates the days from first symptom to treatment by county. Only diagnosis to treatment is measured, and only for the five university hospital areas; the earlier steps are national figures scaled by public county indicators with assumed weights. It is kept as a secondary view (“Time (estimated)”) and is not used in the plan. The check. Spearman rank correlation, across counties, between the estimated days from first symptom to diagnosis (steps 1-4) and three measured outcomes. 0 of 3 outcomes correlate with the estimated clock in the expected direction beyond chance. This is a check, not a validation: it is county-level, with about 22 points, and confounded by age, smoking and stage at diagnosis. The priors were not tuned to improve it. Expected direction: counties with a longer estimated wait have lower share treated with curative intent, moderately (rho -0.30, n 22, permutation p 0.17; could be chance). No relationship: counties with a longer estimated wait do not differ in one-year survival (rho -0.04, n 22). No relationship: counties with a longer estimated wait do not differ in age-standardised lung cancer mortality (rho +0.10, n 23). Reproducible analyses Run with Claude Science from a script. Each one keeps its figures, data, code and every permission it was given, so the result can be re-run. County differences in curative-intent treatment are far larger than chance If every county treated at the national rate of 27.0%, chance alone would put about one county outside the 95% limits. Twelve of 22 are outside. Lapland, South Karelia and Kymenlaakso are below even the 99.8% limits. The seven counties below the limits are together about 50 patients a year short of the national share. This is not adjusted for stage or age, because those are not published per county, so it shows where to look, not why. Full answer, code and data Finland is about ten years behind Sweden and Norway in lung cancer survival, and the gap is growing Men diagnosed with lung cancer in Finland in 2020–2024 have a 5-year relative survival of 17.9%. The Sweden/Norway average passed that level about 10 years ago and is now 31.1%. The gap was close to zero in the 1990s and has widened by about 4 percentage points per decade (95% interval 2.2 to 5.7). For women the gap is 7.9 points, about 6 years. Pancreas and liver show the same pattern. Source: NORDCAN, fetched live by the analysis. Full answer, code and data Limits County-level aggregates cannot show cause. A county with a low share treated to cure is a place to look, not proof of worse care. County shares are not adjusted for stage, fitness or other illness: the registry does not publish those by county. Part of a gap can be treatment that was given but not recorded. Where the registry's own figures suggest that, the county is flagged. Days from diagnosis to treatment are published for the five university hospital areas, not for each county. Effects come from studies in other health systems. No trial has measured them in a Finnish county, and the low end of the access effects is zero. Costs are assumptions and should be replaced with the county's own figures. Åland has too few patients for the registry to publish its care path. Nothing here predicts the course of an individual patient. Three passages of the plan are written by a language model from these numbers, then checked by a second pass that removes any sentence without a source. The table, the targets and the totals are filled in by code. Data sources Opened: we read the number on this page. Listed: we downloaded it but took no number from it.
